## Declarations and implementations

```plato
//==
// # Lines
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Lines — segment measures, projections, and parametric evaluation
//  - Plane, half-space, and slab operations

library Lines
{
    //==
    // # Lines — segment measures, projections, and parametric evaluation
    //
    // The measure, centroid and nearest-point bodies for the segment, line and ray
    // types declared in `lines.types.plato` (`LIBRARIES.md` ground rules 1 and 10: an inline
    // `library` block is the sanctioned home for bodies that belong beside their
    // declarations).
    //
    // Conventions:
    //   * `Bounds` for the two segment types comes from the generic
    //     `Bounds(IPointSet2D/3D)` in `geometry.library.plato`; nothing here
    //     respells it.
    //   * Every `Direction` field is a UNIT vector by its type invariant, so the
    //     projection formulas below divide by no length.

    //==
    // # Line segments

    // The two endpoints, in the segment's own direction (A first).
    Points(s: Line2D): Array<Point2D>
        => [s.A, s.B];

    // The two endpoints, A first.
    Points(s: Line3D): Array<Point3D>
        => [s.A, s.B];

    // The distance between the endpoints.
    Length(s: Line2D): Number
        => s.A.Between(s.B).Magnitude;

    // The distance between the endpoints.
    Length(s: Line3D): Number
        => s.A.Between(s.B).Magnitude;

    // The midpoint: the center of mass of a uniform-density segment.
    Centroid(s: Line2D): Point2D
        => s.A.MidPoint(s.B);

    // The midpoint of the segment.
    Centroid(s: Line3D): Point3D
        => s.A.MidPoint(s.B);

    // The point of the segment nearest to `point` (the projection clamped to the
    // segment's span).
    ClosestPoint(s: Line2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => ClosestPointOnSegment(s.A, s.B, point);

    // The point of the segment nearest to `point`.
    ClosestPoint(s: Line3D, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => ClosestPointOnSegment(s.A, s.B, point);

    // The segment with both endpoints carried through the mapping.
    Deform(s: Line2D, mapping: Function1<Point2D, Point2D>): Line2D
        => (mapping(s.A), mapping(s.B));

    // The segment with both endpoints carried through the mapping.
    Deform(s: Line3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): Line3D
        => (mapping(s.A), mapping(s.B));

    //==
    // # Infinite lines and rays
    //
    // The foot of the perpendicular from `point`: Origin + Direction * t with
    // t = Dot(point - Origin, Direction). The line takes t unrestricted; the ray
    // clamps t to the non-negative half, so a query behind the ray's origin
    // projects onto the origin itself.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_from_a_point_to_a_line

    // The point of the line nearest to `point`.
    ClosestPoint(l: InfiniteLine2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => l.Origin + l.Direction.Vector * l.Origin.Between(point).Dot(l.Direction.Vector);

    // The point of the line nearest to `point`.
    ClosestPoint(l: InfiniteLine3D, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => l.Origin + l.Direction.Vector * l.Origin.Between(point).Dot(l.Direction.Vector);

    // The point of the ray nearest to `point`; the ray's origin when the query
    // lies behind it.
    ClosestPoint(r: Ray2D, point: Point2D): Point2D
        => r.Origin + r.Direction.Vector
            * r.Origin.Between(point).Dot(r.Direction.Vector).Max(0.0);

    // The point of the ray nearest to `point`; the ray's origin when the query
    // lies behind it.
    ClosestPoint(r: Ray3D, point: Point3D): Point3D
        => r.Origin + r.Direction.Vector
            * r.Origin.Between(point).Dot(r.Direction.Vector).Max(0.0);

    //==
    // # Parametric evaluation and inverse
    //
    // `PointAt` maps a parameter to a point; `Parameter` is its inverse, the
    // parameter of the point on the flat NEAREST to a query. Lines take t
    // unrestricted; rays clamp t to the non-negative half; segments run t over
    // [0, 1] between the endpoints (a query off the extent projects to the nearer
    // end). For a line and a ray, `PointAt(x, x.Parameter(p))` equals
    // `x.ClosestPoint(p)`.

    // The point at parameter t: Origin + Direction * t.
    PointAt(l: InfiniteLine2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => l.Origin + l.Direction.Vector * t;

    // The point at parameter t: Origin + Direction * t.
    PointAt(l: InfiniteLine3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => l.Origin + l.Direction.Vector * t;

    // The point at parameter t (t >= 0 lies on the ray): Origin + Direction * t.
    PointAt(r: Ray2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => r.Origin + r.Direction.Vector * t;

    // The point at parameter t (t >= 0 lies on the ray): Origin + Direction * t.
    PointAt(r: Ray3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => r.Origin + r.Direction.Vector * t;

    // The point at parameter t in [0, 1]: A + (B - A) * t.
    PointAt(s: Line2D, t: Number): Point2D
        => s.A.Lerp(s.B, t);

    // The point at parameter t in [0, 1]: A + (B - A) * t.
    PointAt(s: Line3D, t: Number): Point3D
        => s.A.Lerp(s.B, t);

    // The unclamped parameter of the foot of the perpendicular from `point`, so
    // PointAt of it is the line's nearest point. Exact because Direction is unit.
    Parameter(l: InfiniteLine2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => l.Origin.Between(point).Dot(l.Direction.Vector);

    // The unclamped parameter of the foot of the perpendicular from `point`.
    Parameter(l: InfiniteLine3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => l.Origin.Between(point).Dot(l.Direction.Vector);

    // The parameter of `point` clamped to the ray: never negative, so a query
    // behind the origin returns 0.
    Parameter(r: Ray2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => r.Origin.Between(point).Dot(r.Direction.Vector).Max(0.0);

    // The parameter of `point` clamped to the ray.
    Parameter(r: Ray3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => r.Origin.Between(point).Dot(r.Direction.Vector).Max(0.0);

    // The parameter of `point` clamped to [0, 1]: the projection onto the spine
    // A -> B, normalized by the squared span. Degenerate (0/0) only when A equals B.
    Parameter(s: Line2D, point: Point2D): Number
        => (s.A.Between(point).Dot(s.A.Between(s.B)) / s.A.Between(s.B).MagnitudeSquared)
            .Clamp(0.0, 1.0);

    // The parameter of `point` clamped to [0, 1].
    Parameter(s: Line3D, point: Point3D): Number
        => (s.A.Between(point).Dot(s.A.Between(s.B)) / s.A.Between(s.B).MagnitudeSquared)
            .Clamp(0.0, 1.0);
```

## Reading this entry

Parameters before the colon are input values; the type after the parameter list is the result.
The first parameter also supplies the dot-call receiver. Type parameters on a declaration are
bare names; free signature variables use `$`. Read the tier and domain guides for units, frames,
invariants, and the difference between a required interface member and a provided body.
